_about: Canonical question bank for the DayNova Company AI Assessment (the leader path of the DayNova Diagnostic). One leader answers for their team or company. Likert 1-5; reverse items are scored 6 - answer. Pillar max 15, total max 60. scripts/build_report.py reads this file.

stage_question.stem: Is AI in regular, systematic use across your team today?

options.foundation: AI Foundation: Not really. Maybe a few people use ChatGPT or Copilot, but nothing is systematic, owned, or measured.
options.in_practice: AI in Practice: Yes. AI is woven into how some part of our team gets work done, with at least informal ownership and ongoing use.

scale: 1 = Strongly Disagree, 2 = Disagree, 3 = Neutral, 4 = Agree, 5 = Strongly Agree. Answer based on where your team actually is today, not where you're headed.

foundation.label: AI Foundation
foundation.description: Not really. Maybe a few people use ChatGPT or Copilot, but nothing is systematic, owned, or measured.

pillars.title: Narrow
pillars.quote: Tools follow strategy. Not the other way around.

questions.text: Our leadership has aligned on where we should adopt AI first, and why.
We've identified the specific outcomes AI needs to deliver before we evaluate tools.
We add new tools and platforms faster than we retire old ones.

pillars.title: Orchestrate
pillars.quote: You can't plug AI into chaos and call it transformation.

questions.text: Our team has a shared, explicit understanding of how core work flows from idea to delivery today.
There is a clear point of accountability for AI decisions in our organization.
Processes differ from team to team, with little or no standardization.

pillars.title: Validate
pillars.quote: If you don't define good before AI lands, AI defines it for you.

questions.text: We have shared standards for what good looks like in our content, decisions, and deliverables.
Our team has discussed the brand, compliance, and accuracy risks AI poses to our specific work.
We have a defined review process for high-stakes work before it goes out the door.

pillars.title: Amplify
pillars.quote: AI without ambition just produces more of the same.

questions.text: Our leadership treats AI as a capacity multiplier for strategic work, not just a cost-cutting tool.
Our team can articulate the strategic work we'd take on if execution capacity doubled.
We measure our team on output volume more than on strategic outcomes.

bands.name: Pre-Foundation
bands.title: You're in the Pre-Foundation band.
bands.blurb: You haven't done the strategic groundwork. Tools won't fix this, thinking will. The fastest move is a leadership alignment workshop to define priorities, ownership, and success.

bands.name: Foundation-Building
bands.title: You're in the Foundation-Building band.
bands.blurb: You've started the thinking. The gap is between intent and operational rollout. Advisory engagement turns your direction into a concrete plan with owners, milestones, and guardrails.

bands.name: Foundation-Ready
bands.title: You're in the Foundation-Ready band.
bands.blurb: You're ready to deploy. The next leverage isn't more discussion, it's a structured pilot. An AI Reboot Camp turns your alignment into adoption with the right people, tools, and feedback loops.

in_practice.label: AI in Practice
in_practice.description: Yes. AI is woven into how some part of our team gets work done, with at least informal ownership and ongoing use.

pillars.title: Narrow
pillars.quote: The teams that win won't be the ones doing the most. They'll be the ones doing the right things.

questions.text: When we bring on a new AI tool, we take time to define what success looks like before we get started.
Our team has a shared understanding of which decisions belong to humans and which are great candidates for AI support.
We currently have more AI tools running than we have clear owners or defined use cases for.

pillars.title: Orchestrate
pillars.quote: Work is a team sport. AI is a new team member. Does your team have clear roles, clear handoffs, and clear owners?

questions.text: Our team has a clear picture of how people collaborate and hand off work across our core workflows.
We know where AI tools plug into our process and who is responsible for each one.
Different team members use different AI tools for the same types of tasks, without a shared approach or standard.

pillars.title: Validate
pillars.quote: Speed without judgment isn't efficiency. It's liability.

questions.text: We have a consistent, shared approach to reviewing AI-generated content (written, visual, or otherwise) before it goes live.
Our team feels confident spotting when AI output misses the mark, whether that's a factual error, an off-brand tone, or a flawed recommendation.
Our prompts are reliable enough that we rarely feel the need to review AI outputs before they go live.

pillars.title: Amplify
pillars.quote: AI should expand what's possible, not just replace what was.

questions.text: AI has created meaningful capacity on our team that we actively reinvest in bigger-picture, strategic work.
We're producing more, or meaningfully better, output than we were 12 months ago, without adding headcount.
We can point to real, measurable business outcomes that improved directly because of how our team adopted AI.

bands.name: In Practice, Fragmented
bands.title: You're in the In Practice, Fragmented band.
bands.blurb: You're using AI, but adoption is uneven and discipline is missing. A workshop creates the shared standards and ownership that turn scattered usage into systematic capability.

bands.name: In Practice, Transitioning
bands.title: You're in the In Practice, Transitioning band.
bands.blurb: You've got real adoption. The risk now is scaling the wrong behaviors. Advisory engagement tightens the operating model before fragmentation locks in.

bands.name: In Practice, Amplifying
bands.title: You're in the In Practice, Amplifying band.
bands.blurb: You're ahead of most. The next leverage is custom workflows that compound the advantage. We build the integrations that turn capability into a durable edge.
